mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where CPI YoY growth exceeds 3% and FEDFUNDS subsequently rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and increased consumer spending, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5% month-over-month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE declines by more than 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO declines by more than 2% month-over-month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a single month signals strong job growth, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased investment and borrowing, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS declines by more than 0.25%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds 3% quarter-over-quarter and is accompanied by a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong economic growth and increased demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ growth > 3% and INDPRO MoM growth > 1%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 QoQ growth exceeds 3% and INDPRO MoM growth exceeds 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.
